subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the straight line perpendicular to the line 5x−3y+1=0 and passing through the point (4,−3).

mark_split.label: Write the line through the point

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.81 — VSAQ chapter 14 Straight Lines, answer 92.2. recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what the slope must be, and which form you would use.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the required slope
steps.margin_note: First mark. Read the given line's slope off its coefficients as −a/b, then flip and negate it, because perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
steps.memory_tip: Read the slope off as −a/b, then FLIP AND NEGATE — perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.

recall.must_convey: That the given slope is found as −a/b and the required slope is −1/m.
accept: perpendicular so take minus one over the slope
flip and negate the given slope
the perpendicular slope is minus one by m
perpendicular kabatti minus one by m

steps.why: The slope is fixed entirely by the other line, so it can be written before the given point is used at all.
common_mistakes: Keeping the same slope, which gives a parallel line instead.

steps.label: Write the line through the point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Point-slope form, then clear the fraction and collect. There is also a one-line shortcut for this shape, given below.
steps.memory_tip: Point-slope form through the given point, then clear and collect.
lines: Perpendicular through (4, −3) with slope −3/5 is  y − y₁ = (−1/m)(x − x₁)
The perpendicular line is given by  b(x − x₁) − a(y − y₁) = 0

recall.must_convey: That the point-slope form through the given point gives 3x + 5y + 3 = 0.
accept: use y minus y one equals m into x minus x one then simplify
write the point slope form and clear the fraction
put the point and slope in and collect the terms
point slope form lo pettesi simplify cheyyali

steps.why: The shortcut works because a perpendicular line keeps the same coefficients swapped with one sign changed, so only the constant has to be recomputed.
common_mistakes: Sign slip when the point has a negative coordinate.
Leaving the answer with a fraction in it.

insider_note: The short route is b(x − x₁) − a(y − y₁) = 0, which swaps the coefficients and flips one sign — no reciprocal needed. The point's y is −3, so that bracket is (y + 3).
